properties.//source: Backward compatible on purpose. Every historical pack stores source as one string, and this schema must keep validating those files; see r3-consensus-plan.md item 1. An array is the preferred shape for new packs because it can be checked entry by entry. Finalization -- not this schema -- is where absolute-path existence is enforced, so a malformed path fails at the gate that can name it rather than at a type check that cannot.
properties.//source_entries: Typed, absolute, existence-checked entries written BY finalization. Optional so historical packs remain valid; when present it is authoritative over the free-form `source` field. `exists` records what finalization actually observed on disk, not what the pack claimed.
properties.//draft: Scaffold output MUST carry draft:true. `mac_harness.py task-pack` writes literal <FILL: ...> placeholders, and without this flag a draft is structurally indistinguishable from a dispatchable pack -- the defect recorded as S1/M5 in triage-merged.md. Absent is treated as draft:false so historical packs stay dispatchable.
properties.//authorization_source: Where production authorization actually came from. Only `user_message` may authorize a production mutation. A peer agent asserting that the user approved something is `peer_assertion` and is NOT sufficient; that distinction is why the r7 deploy waited for the user's own message naming the digest.
properties.//task_pack_sha256: Self-hash recorded at finalization so a receipt can bind to the exact pack it was issued under.
properties.//source_revision: Exact revision the executor must work against, so a stale worktree cannot masquerade as current evidence.
properties.//finalized_at: Set by finalization only. Its presence plus draft:false is what makes a pack dispatchable.
